speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, a celebration in appreciation of the efforts put by our teachers should not just be tied to a single day, but we should explore a month-long celebration and more importantly, a lifelong recognition.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: On this note, I would like to record my appreciation to my Primary school teachers from Mei Chin Primary School, from the cohort of 1979 to 1984, and from Yusof Ishak Secondary School, cohort 1985 to 1988.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This group of teachers taught me not just academic subjects, but also moral education and values, that I hold on until today.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Of the many teachers, one that remains a strong memory is my Secondary school form teacher Mr Cherry Chacko, who taught me English and Literature.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, he was the one that gave me the opportunity at such a young age of 15 years old, to address the school during assembly, an opportunity and experience that I will never forget till today.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Not forgetting all my other teachers from both Primary and Secondary school: Teachers, without your dedication and commitment to educate me with the right values, I would not be able to be where I am today, both as a principal technical officer and a union leader in the power industry.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I strongly believe and affirm that no student is allowed to disrespect their teacher and what more to threaten in such nature?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I have a feeling that such an incident of that nature is not an isolated one or few, but there is so much more.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, I do hear similar stories of teachers experiencing similar disrespectful moments.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Whilst preparing my content for this Motion, I recently reached out to my fellow union leaders from the Singapore Teachers' Union, Singapore Malay Teachers' Union, Singapore Chinese Teachers' Union and also Singapore Tamil Teachers' Union.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, there are many more that represent educators from early childhood to Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The grievances and feedbacks range from managing students' behaviour, abusive attacks from students' parents, work appraisal, mental health and on a lighter note, career progression.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The unions acknowledged that MOE had been supportive towards them in resolving conflicts and take feedbacks positively on salary scale and career progression.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This announcement signifies MOE's continuous commitment to constantly monitor and review the teachers' salaries, welfare and work prospects.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Notwithstanding the above, the unions believe that MOE could do more in terms of policies to address teachers' concerns and hence, setting policies that would at least set a baseline for school practices.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Further, MOE ought to expect school leadership to support teachers more and better.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe it is the school leadership which is the fulcrum.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: More support must be given to teachers by school leaders, MOE and we ourselves as parents.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Students must be made aware and reminded continuously that any misbehaviours, rudeness, aggressiveness, or worse, threats, will never be condoned and they must face equal-like consequences.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The school leadership must support the teachers in disciplining students and stand firm when communicating with parents on disciplinary matters.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: While approaches to disciplining matters may differ, teachers must feel that these approaches are effective with the strong backing of school leadership.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We must ensure that the dignity of teachers is maintained and that the restorative practices are also implemented to resolve conflict, repair harm and heal relationships.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This is also to maintain and uphold the students' dignity and well-being.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Our teachers have their personal lives and family to attend to.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We, as parents, need to understand that teachers need their work-life balance as much as us.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Even with this, the teachers would always go beyond the call of duty.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, parents must always respect teachers' private space and time.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Parents can play a role in becoming constructive and complementary partners of teachers to support the students' growth and development.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The final one is about reducing teachers' workload and calibrated expectations.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: As teaching becomes increasingly complex and there are competing demands on teachers' time, more could be done for this final area.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Teachers need more time outside of classroom teaching to attend to marking, preparing for lessons and working on student guidance.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The expectations must be calibrated vis-a-vis ranking and appraisal as well as reducing non-teaching-related workload ought to be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: As teachers go beyond the call of duty, it is even more vital that there is curtailing of teachers' official duties and calibration of expectations.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   The recent incident between a student and a school teacher is quite disturbing and worrying.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Throughout my experience as a student in a neighbourhood school, fights and similar incidents are common among students, be it within my school or in other schools.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: But we could never have imagined an era where students disrespect their teachers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This is totally unacceptable, and as parents, we should be ashamed if our children behave that way.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Parents must be firm in educating our children so that they respect their teachers, instead of doing the opposite.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I would like to share this Malay quatrain, which emphasises the importance of students always showing respect to their teachers, because teachers are the providers of knowledge.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In preparing my speech, I have also engaged and obtained feedback from my union colleagues as well as my acquaintances who are teachers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: It is sad and heart-breaking to hear their issues and grievances arising from the challenges of handling the discipline of school students, parental interference, encroachment of their personal hours outside school hours and many more.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: There are also those who have not seen any improvement in their career progression after several years.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, this was changed recently when MOE made policy revisions in relation to teachers' careers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure that the challenges I mentioned have received MOE's attention and support, and at the same time, MOE should be more cognizant of teachers' contributions and not place excessive responsibility on teachers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I appeal to MOE and school principals to think about this issue and find the best solution.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, to trade union representatives, you should always approach your union members who are teachers in order to listen and receive feedback about their challenges and expectations as a teacher.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Specially for all our esteemed teachers, I would like to share another Malay quatrain as a tribute to your service – which states that I received so much from my teachers, and those memories remain after all these years.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This gesture is also similar given by MOH for all their healthcare personnel in managing the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: To the parents out there, continue educating our children to always respect their teachers and most importantly, please, parents, respect the teachers' privacy and time.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Avoid sending any unnecessary messages beyond school hours, if we believe that we, as career-minded parents, need work-life balance, the teachers need that too.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I quote, "The duties of a teacher are neither few nor small, but they elevate the mind and they give energy to the character." On that note, every teacher matters!

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Our teachers and educators join the profession and make it a career out of a passion to nurture and build up our young and the next generation.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Notwithstanding, this round of salary review and adjustments by MOE will help in some way to ensure their remuneration remains competitive.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This is a positive development as many teachers and educators prefer and are more passionate to do teaching as their main job and competency instead of the administrative or leadership path.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: However, I opine that remuneration alone is not something which will automatically attract or retain them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There are other areas, such as career progression, learning and development opportunities as well as the work environment, be it good supervisors, supportive colleagues and understanding parents of students all play a part to attract and retain our educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In this respect, I think more can also be done to ensure the mental well-being of our educators including SPED educators and pre-school educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: First, educators should be given opportunities to go on sabbaticals and also gap years to go on industry attachments outside of the education service, such as the people and private sector, to recharge and refresh their knowledge and perspectives.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second, I am aware teachers spend loads of time setting and preparing exam scripts for continual and semestral exams, including the upcoming for prelims.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This will reduce disparity and take a whole load of onerous time off teachers and schools with this co-sharing of exam script preparation.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Third, speaking on behalf of Union of ITE Training Staff (UITS), Ngee Ann Polytechnic Academic Staff Union (NPASU), Amalgamated Union of Public Employees (AUPE), The Singapore Manual & Mercantile Workers' Union (SMMWU) and Education Services Union (ESU), I hope that the same can also be extended to our educators in the Polytechnics, ITEs and all other educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We hope that the rest of the players in the private education sphere, which includes early childhood, student care, Autonomous Universities and Private Education Institutes (PEIs), will also do likewise and review their salaries to ensure that their overall salary packages remain competitive, and also to help those who need to cope with the rising cost of living.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am also aware some of the PEI trainers and lecturers are independent contractors also known as gig workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: A review of their compensation and benefits is also timely.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: All these will go a long way to give an assurance to our educators that, whether they are from the public and or the private sectors, their role in educating our future generations is recognised and valued.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There are minimal progression opportunities for this group of educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I hope that we can do more to uplift the profession of this group of educators and help raise the salary and progression of these student care educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I know our Education Services Union will be happy and willing to work together with them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In fact, ESU is already working with some companies in the student care sector on the Company Training Committee initiative and we hope that bigger players will also come on board.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In MOE, it is often said of our teachers: "Through your hands passes the future of our nation".

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A teacher's responsibility is a great one, as it involves moulding students and shaping lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE appreciates the significance of the work of our educators and we are committed to ensuring their well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are particularly grateful to our educators who worked tirelessly as frontliners over the past two years of COVID-19 pandemic, keeping schools open and safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This significantly reduced the impact of school closures and disruptions on the learning and well-being of our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The outcomes will be shared with their staff when the review is completed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While paying our educators competitively is important, building a quality teaching service goes beyond salaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE is committed to supporting the well-being and development of our educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On the issue of students' discipline, our educators' work goes beyond just teaching in the classroom to inculcating good values and character in our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE has set out guidelines for schools to formulate their own discipline policies and approaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: School Leaders take a strong stand against disrespectful behaviour towards teachers and strive to promote a safe and supportive school environment for all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When engaging parents, our teachers accord appropriate respect and courtesy, and the same is expected of parents in their interactions with our teachers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When parents use abusive words or threaten teachers, School Leaders will communicate a firm stand against such behaviour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE HR works closely with the teachers' unions to support the well-being of our educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have quarterly dialogues to discuss matters such as capacity building, mental well-being support and grievance handling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The unions also provide an additional source of feedback on ground issues and highlight specific cases of educators who require stronger support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Managing our educators' workload is an important area of focus in MOE.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To create capacity for educators, our schools are also resourced with additional staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Every school has a team of Allied Educators who perform various functions, such as counselling and working with students with special educational needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: All schools have a School Administration Team that performs administrative and operational functions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Schools are given additional posts and funding which they can use flexibly to meet their needs by hiring more staff to help with administrative roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE also provides funding for schools to engage vendors to help with event planning and conducting after-school enrichment activities and camps, though teachers will still need to exercise oversight and provide the duty of care for their students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To support work-life harmony for educators, our schools and education institutions have introduced more flexible work arrangements for educators where feasible, while maintaining the duty of care towards students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This includes holding virtual or hybrid parent-teacher meetings and staff meetings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Educators who require greater flexibility in working hours can also apply for part-time teaching arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: During school holidays, all schools provide Protected Vacation Time for educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This ensures that educators have time to rest and recharge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: An enabling school environment built on a culture of trust and support is key to our educators' well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: School Leaders and supervisors proactively check in with their officers regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Educators are encouraged to share their concerns with their supervisors and leaders, or with the Superintendent overseeing their school.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, they can tap on other channels for support, such as their school's Wellness Ambassadors, MOE's in-house professional counselling services and the 24/7 whole-of-Government Counselling Hotline for public officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Schools' Staff Well-Being Committees have been provided with more resources to enhance staff well-being, such as additional funds and in-house curated resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Educators can also take part in well-being workshops and talks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beyond these measures, parents play a significant role in supporting educators' well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, parents could respect educators' personal time by minimising non-critical communication with them outside work hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Give schools and educators some time to respond to your queries and feedback.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have started a good movement with the Parent Support Groups (PSGs) in our schools as we continue to strengthen our partnership with parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I am grateful for how our PSGs are forging ahead in complementing our schools' efforts in doing more for our students and fellow parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, Fuhua Primary School's PSG, led by Mdm Tse Ka Po and her team, has been carrying out various initiatives for their parent community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There is Junior Gems One Ninety (JnrGEMS1:90), a parent buddy programme that connects senior parents to incoming Primary 1 parents to share experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There is also a chat group, ConnectGEMS, for parents to support one another on class-based issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Both platforms are facilitated by PSG EXCO members who send reminders on school matters as well as share information on volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This PSG initiative sets a constructive tone in every class's parent chat group and relieves educators from responding to questions that are frequently asked by parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We can all support our educators by showing appreciation for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Hilda's Primary School: "Thank you for going above and beyond, everytime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For looking out and cheering our children every day, celebrating small achievements and assuring that every win is an accomplishment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are grateful and very blessed to have you as our Form Teacher." We would like to thank everyone for encouraging our educators with your words of appreciation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These heart-warming messages show how much our educators are valued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We care for their well-being and will continue to work with all stakeholders, including School Leaders, parents and the community, to support them.
